## Bio!
Growing up, the bill was scarier than the illness. My family immigrated without 
health insurance, so regular medical care was out of reach. When my dad had a 
heart attack, I couldn't stop wondering. If we'd had insurance, would this have 
happen at all? That question shaped my path toward interest in preventive 
cardiology and immigrant health. 

I am a part-time MPH student at the Johns Hopkins School of Public Health, 
concentrating in Epidemiology and Biostatistic. I hope to become a clinician 
and clinical epidemiologist who uses population-level research to improve 
cardiovascular outcomes for particularly underserved communities. I’m 
particularly interested in hypertension management, novel biomarkers, and 
community outreach in the context of cardiology. 

Please feel free to download my complete CV to see my research experience,
clinical experience, and public health experience.
